standard_prerequisites.use: Morphisms-chapter flatness of smooth maps and base change of smooth maps; Divisors, lemma section-smooth-regular-immersion; the chapter's regular-immersion-lci and lci-properties lemmas; Divided Power Algebra, lemma perfect-diagonal (a perfect diagonal plus flatness forces smoothness in the Noetherian finite type setting).

core_obligations: Prove the diagonal of a smooth map is a section of a smooth projection.
Chain regular immersion -> lci -> perfect via the named chapter lemmas.
Close the cycle with the divided-powers perfect-diagonal theorem.

proof_roadmap.step: Forward implications via standard diagonal-as-section arguments.

difficulty_reason: For a finite type morphism f : X -> Y of locally Noetherian schemes with diagonal Delta, the lemma gives four equivalent conditions: f smooth; f flat with Delta a regular immersion; f flat with Delta a local complete intersection morphism; f flat with Delta perfect. The retained proof is written as a short chain: (1) => (2) because a smooth map is flat (cited Morphisms lemma smooth-flat), the projections of X x_Y X onto X are smooth (base-change-smooth), and the diagonal is a section of a smooth morphism hence a regular immersion (Divisors, lemma section-smooth-regular-immersion); (2) => (3) and (3) => (4) are the chapter's own lemma-regular-immersion-lci and lemma-lci-properties; (4) => (1) is the punchline, Divided Power Algebra, lemma perfect-diagonal, cited as the interesting implication. Retained author proof at lines 18542-18556.

dedup.scope: Four-way smoothness equivalence through flatness plus a regular/lci/perfect diagonal.
